subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Listening for specific information; grouping words (Top Tip)
outcomes: Listen for specific information in a dialogue
Group words with related meanings into lexical fields

tf.why: Yes, he is in his last year of school.

tf.s: In London, the father thinks Majid would speak English all the time.
tf.why: He thinks Majid would speak Arabic with friends in London.

tf.s: Majid's father prefers London to Chichester.
Chichester is a small city near the sea.
tf.why: That is one of its advantages.

tf.s: Chichester has a direct rail link to London.
tf.why: So Majid can travel to London easily.

tf.s: The father thinks Majid will speak English with local people in Chichester.
A lexical field is a group of words connected by meaning.
tf.why: For example, words about university life.

tf.s: 'Campus', 'lecture' and 'degree' belong to the lexical field of cooking.
Grouping words by topic can help you remember vocabulary.
tf.why: Words in groups are easier to remember.

tf.s: Before listening, it is best not to read the statements.
tf.why: Reading first tells you what to listen for.
